mainTopic: תמורה: Who can make a substitution, whether it is permitted, and the dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה about an heir doing סמיכה and תמורה
overview: The משנה opens מסכת תמורה. It teaches that everyone, men and women, can swap a regular animal for a consecrated one. Doing so is forbidden, but if someone does it, the swap works and he gets מלקות. The גמרא first asks whether 'everyone substitutes' means it is allowed לכתחילה. It shows that reading is impossible, because a פסוק forbids תמורה. רב יהודה then explains that 'everyone' simply has the power to make holiness take hold through תמורה. Next the גמרא asks whom the word הכל adds, and answers: an heir. This follows רבי מאיר and not רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה says an heir can do neither סמיכה nor תמורה, learning the start of הקדש from its end. סמיכה is learned from the three times the תורה says 'קרבנו', and the גמרא explains how each side uses those words, including for partners. Finally, רבי מאיר learns from the doubled verb הָמֵר יָמִיר that an heir can do תמורה.

steps.title: The משנה: Everyone can do substitution, but it is not permitted
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that both men and women can do תמורה. It is not permitted, but if done, it takes effect and the person receives forty lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Everyone can substitute, both men and women. This does not mean a person is allowed to substitute. Rather, if he did substitute, the substitution takes effect, and he receives the forty lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה states the basic rule of תמורה: anyone, man or woman, can swap a regular animal for a consecrated one. It also warns that doing so is forbidden and is punished with lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two ideas sit side by side. Doing תמורה actually works, so the new animal becomes holy too. Yet the act itself is a sin that carries מלקות. The משנה adds the second line so no one thinks 'everyone substitutes' means it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: They substitute: swapping a regular animal for a consecrated one, so the regular one becomes holy too
Permitted, allowed
Here: it is substituted, meaning the swap takes effect
He absorbs the forty: he receives מלקות (lashes) for breaking a לאו

steps.confusionAlert: Here מוּמָר does NOT mean a heretic or someone who abandoned the תורה, which is its common meaning elsewhere. In this משנה it simply means 'the substitution took effect.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the central idea of the whole מסכת. תמורה is forbidden, yet it works and creates real holiness.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: Everyone can substitute
phrases.notes: To substitute means to declare a regular animal a replacement for a consecrated one.

phrases.english: both men and women.
Not that a person is permitted to substitute,
rather, that if he did substitute, it is substituted,
phrases.notes: In other words, the swap works: both animals are now holy.

phrases.english: and he receives the forty lashes.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone, men and women, has the power to do תמורה. It is forbidden, but if done it takes effect and the person receives מלקות.

steps.title: The משנה seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that 'everyone substitutes' sounds לכתחילה, while 'if he substituted it takes effect' sounds דיעבד.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: This משנה itself is difficult. You said 'everyone substitutes', which sounds like it is allowed from the start. Then it teaches 'not that a person is permitted to substitute, but if he substituted it takes effect', which sounds like after the fact only!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה from within itself. The first line and the second line seem to say opposite things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'everyone substitutes' sound like describing a normal, allowed activity. The next line says it is only valid after it was wrongly done. So which is it?

keyTerms.meaning: This itself is difficult: a challenge showing a text contradicts itself
From the outset: allowed to be done in the first place
After the fact: not allowed, but valid once done

phrases.english: GEMARA: This itself is difficult:
You said 'everyone substitutes', meaning from the outset,
and then it teaches
'not that a person is permitted to substitute,
rather that if he substituted it takes effect', meaning only after the fact!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the internal consistency of the משנה in step 1.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first clause implies תמורה is allowed לכתחילה, while the second clause says it is valid only דיעבד, so the two clauses contradict.

steps.title: The question's starting assumption cannot be right, because the verse forbids substitution
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that 'everyone substitutes' could mean לכתחילה, since a פסוק explicitly forbids תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think 'everyone substitutes' means it is allowed from the outset? Before you ask from the משנה, ask from the verse! It is written: 'He shall not exchange it, nor substitute it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the question itself. 'Everyone substitutes' could never mean it is allowed, because the תורה clearly forbids it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was not a contradiction between two lines of the משנה. The reading of the first line was simply wrong. If 'everyone substitutes' meant 'allowed', it would clash with the פסוק, and no משנה would say that. So the first line must mean something else, which sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you even think so? Used to reject an assumption

keyTerms.term: אַדְּקַשְׁיָא לָךְ מִמַּתְנִיתִין תִּיקְשֵׁי לָךְ קְרָא
keyTerms.meaning: Before the משנה troubles you, the פסוק should trouble you: you are pointing at the smaller problem
He shall not exchange it nor substitute it: the verse forbidding תמורה

phrases.english: And can you really think that 'everyone substitutes' means from the outset?
Before it is difficult for you from the Mishnah,
let the verse be difficult for you!
As it is written: 'He shall not exchange it, nor substitute it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the premise of the question in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The assumption that 'הכל ממירין' means substitution is allowed לכתחילה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That reading contradicts an explicit פסוק forbidding תמורה, so it cannot be what the משנה means.

steps.title: רב יהודה explains: everyone has the power to make holiness take hold through substitution
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reads 'everyone substitutes' as 'everyone can make holiness take hold through תמורה', not as permission to do it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יהודה said: This is what the משנה teaches. Everyone can make holiness take hold through substitution, both men and women. That does not mean a person is allowed to substitute. For if he substitutes, it takes effect, and he receives the forty lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives the correct meaning of the משנה. 'Everyone substitutes' is about ability, not permission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By rewording 'ממירין' as 'מתפיסין בתמורה', רב יהודה shows that the first line talks about power. Anyone's תמורה makes the new animal holy. The second line then explains that this power works even though using it is a sin. So there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches: introduces a reworded explanation of a text
They make holiness take hold (on another animal)
Substitution: swapping a regular animal for a consecrated one

steps.whatToRemember: 'הכל ממירין' means everyone has the POWER to do תמורה, so it takes effect. It does not mean it is allowed. Doing it is a לאו punished with forty lashes.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yehuda said:
This is what it teaches:
Everyone can make holiness take hold through substitution,
both men and women;
not that a person is permitted to substitute,
for if he substituted, it takes effect,
and he receives the forty lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה הָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 3 showed the 'לכתחילה' reading is impossible, רב יהודה supplies the correct reading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'הכל ממירין' seemed to mean that substitution is permitted לכתחילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'הכל ממירין' means everyone has the power to transfer holiness through תמורה. The act is forbidden and punished with lashes, but it takes effect.

steps.title: What does the word 'everyone' come to include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the word הכל in the משנה is adding.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Everyone' — who does that come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the word הכל ('everyone') in the משנה and asks what extra person it is meant to include. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word like 'everyone' looks extra, since the משנה could have just said that men and women do תמורה. The גמרא assumes the extra word must be there to add some case that we might have left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone; a broad word that usually adds an extra case
To include; to bring in an extra case

phrases.english: 'Everyone' comes to include what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the word הכל from the משנה and asks a new question about what it includes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which extra person the word הכל includes in the law of תמורה.

steps.title: It includes an heir, against רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: הכל includes a יורש, so the משנה does not follow רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include an heir, and this is not like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'everyone' includes a יורש, a person who inherited a קרבן. It adds that this means the משנה disagrees with רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally only the person who made the animal holy would be able to do תמורה on it. The word הכל teaches that even an heir can. Since רבי יהודה says an heir cannot, the משנה must follow a different opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: An heir; here, someone who inherited an animal that his father made holy
And not in line with (the opinion of)

phrases.english: To include an heir,
and not in line with רבי יהודה.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הכל includes a יורש, which shows the משנה is not following רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The source: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue about an heir
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the dispute: רבי מאיר says an heir does סמיכה and תמורה; רבי יהודה says he does neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: An heir does סמיכה, and an heir does תמורה — the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: an heir does not do סמיכה and does not do תמורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source showing that רבי יהודה holds an heir cannot do תמורה. This backs up the claim that our משנה does not follow him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dispute covers two laws together: סמיכה (leaning hands on the קרבן) and תמורה. רבי מאיר lets an heir act like the original owner in both; רבי יהודה lets him do neither. Our משנה, which includes the heir, matches רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Does סמיכה — leans his hands on the head of the קרבן before it is slaughtered
Does תמורה — tries to swap a regular animal for a holy one

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: an heir does סמיכה and תמורה. רבי יהודה: an heir does neither. Our משנה follows רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: As we learned: An heir does סמיכה,
an heir does תמורה — the words of רבי מאיר.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: יוֹרֵשׁ אֵינוֹ סוֹמֵךְ,
phrases.english: רבי יהודה says: An heir does not do סמיכה,
and an heir does not do תמורה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the claim in step 6 that רבי יהודה disagrees.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה's inclusion of an heir is not in line with רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching recording the dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה about an heir doing סמיכה and תמורה.

steps.title: Why does רבי יהודה say an heir cannot do תמורה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רבי יהודה's reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה holds that an heir cannot do תמורה. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An heir now owns the animal, so it seems he should be able to do whatever an owner does. The גמרא wants to know what source or logic makes רבי יהודה exclude him.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of רבי יהודה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רבי יהודה's view quoted in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or logic for רבי יהודה's ruling that an heir cannot do תמורה.

steps.title: He learns the start of הקדש from its end
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה compares תמורה (start of הקדש) to סמיכה (end of הקדש): just as an heir does no סמיכה, he does no תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns the start of הקדש from the end of הקדש: just as at the end of הקדש an heir does not do סמיכה, so too at the start of הקדש an heir does not do תמורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רבי יהודה compares two stages of a holy animal. Since an heir cannot do סמיכה at the end, he also cannot do תמורה at the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תמורה makes a new animal holy, so it belongs to the 'start' of holiness. סמיכה is done right before the קרבן is offered, at the 'end'. רבי יהודה says the heir is left out of both stages in the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns (one law from another)
The start of holiness — making an animal holy, like through תמורה
The end of holiness — the offering stage, where סמיכה is done

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two stages: תמורה is the 'start' (it creates holiness), and סמיכה is the 'end' (done when the קרבן is brought).

phrases.english: He learns the start of הקדש from the end of הקדש:

phrases.aramaic: מָה סוֹף הֶקְדֵּשׁ — יוֹרֵשׁ אֵינוֹ סוֹמֵךְ,
phrases.english: just as at the end of הקדש, an heir does not do סמיכה,

phrases.aramaic: אַף תְּחִילַּת הֶקְדֵּשׁ — יוֹרֵשׁ אֵינוֹ מֵמִיר.
phrases.english: so too at the start of הקדש, an heir does not do תמורה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by giving רבי יהודה's comparison.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה compares the start of הקדש (תמורה) to the end of הקדש (סמיכה), where an heir is excluded.

steps.title: Where do we learn that an heir does no סמיכה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the סמיכה rule itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And סמיכה itself — where do we learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where we know that an heir does no סמיכה, since רבי יהודה's comparison depends on it. This sets up the source in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison in step 9 only works if the 'end' rule is already proven. So the גמרא checks the foundation: what source excludes an heir from סמיכה?

keyTerms.meaning: Itself
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: And סמיכה itself — from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the סמיכה rule that step 9 relied on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches an heir does not do סמיכה.

steps.title: Three times 'his offering' — not a gentile, not a friend, not a father
steps.stepSummary: The word קרבנו is written three times; each one excludes someone from סמיכה, and the third excludes an heir.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'His offering' is written three times: one — 'his offering' and not a gentile's offering; one — 'his offering' and not his friend's offering; and one — 'his offering' and not his father's offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוקים about סמיכה say 'קרבנו' three times. Each time removes one person, and the last one removes an heir doing סמיכה on his father's קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'His offering' means only the owner leans on it. The three mentions teach three exclusions: a non-Jew, someone else's קרבן, and a father's קרבן that the son inherited. That last one is the 'end of הקדש' rule רבי יהודה builds on.

keyTerms.meaning: His offering — the word the פסוק uses for the קרבן one does סמיכה on
Three are written; the word appears three times
His friend; another person

steps.whatToRemember: Three times 'קרבנו' exclude a gentile, another person, and a father's קרבן from סמיכה. The last one is רבי יהודה's base for saying an heir cannot do תמורה either.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the chain: הכל includes an heir (רבי מאיר), while רבי יהודה excludes him based on סמיכה, which is learned from 'קרבנו'.

phrases.english: 'His offering' is written three times:
one — 'his offering' and not a gentile's offering,
and one — 'his offering' and not his friend's offering,
and one — 'his offering' and not his father's offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 with the פסוק source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The three mentions of 'קרבנו' exclude a gentile, another person, and a father's קרבן, so an heir does no סמיכה.

steps.title: Challenge to רבי מאיר from the third קרבנו
steps.stepSummary: If רבי מאיר says an heir does סמיכה, what does he do with the third קרבנו, which seems to exclude an heir?
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי מאיר says an heir does סמיכה. Isn't the word 'his offering' written?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי מאיר and challenges him. The extra word קרבנו seems to exclude an heir from סמיכה, so how can רבי מאיר say an heir does it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11, the third קרבנו was used to exclude an heir. רבי מאיר says the opposite, so he must explain what that third word teaches him. Otherwise the word looks extra in his view.

keyTerms.meaning: an heir, someone who inherited the animal from the owner
leaning one's hands on the animal's head before it is brought as a קרבן
'his offering', a word in the פסוק written three times
'but isn't it written…?', used to raise a challenge from a פסוק

phrases.english: But according to רבי מאיר, who says an heir does סמיכה,
isn't 'his offering' written?!
phrases.notes: He means the third קרבנו, the one used in step 11 to leave out an heir.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּאָמַר יוֹרֵשׁ סוֹמֵךְ, וְהָכְתִיב ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the derivation from step 11 against רבי מאיר's opposing view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's ruling that an heir does סמיכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The third קרבנו excludes an heir, so רבי מאיר's ruling seems to go against the פסוק.

steps.title: רבי מאיר uses the third קרבנו for partners
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר needs the third קרבנו to teach that all partners in an animal must do סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs that word to include all the partners in סמיכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי מאיר. He uses the third קרבנו for a different lesson, so it is not available to exclude an heir.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, the third קרבנו includes rather than excludes: every partner in a shared קרבן must lean his hands on it. Since the word is used up, nothing excludes an heir.

keyTerms.meaning: he needs it (this word) for a different lesson
to include, to add a case into the rule
partners, several people who own one קרבן together

phrases.english: He needs that one
to include all partners in סמיכה.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the extra word to a different lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The third קרבנו must exclude an heir.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי מאיר, the third קרבנו includes partners in סמיכה, so it does not exclude an heir.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: partners do not do סמיכה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה does not hold that partners do סמיכה, because a shared קרבן does not belong to one person.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה does not hold that partners do סמיכה. Why? Because their קרבן does not belong to one person alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי יהודה deals with partners. He uses the third קרבנו to exclude an heir, so in this answer he simply holds that partners do not do סמיכה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is that קרבנו means 'his own' offering. A shared קרבן is not 'his' alone, so partners are not covered.

keyTerms.meaning: he does not hold this
belonging to one specific person

phrases.english: And רבי יהודה,
does not hold that partners do סמיכה.
What is the reason?
Because their offering does not belong to just one of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, בַּעֲלֵי חוֹבְרִין לִסְמִיכָה לֵית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 13 used the third קרבנו for partners. This step answers how רבי יהודה, who needs all three for exclusions, handles partners: he does not require סמיכה for them. Step 15 offers a second answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, partners do not do סמיכה, because a shared קרבן is not 'his' offering.

steps.title: Second answer: רבי יהודה does include partners
steps.stepSummary: Or: רבי יהודה does hold that partners do סמיכה. He learns the gentile and the friend from one קרבנו, which frees up a word for partners.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you could say: he really does hold that partners do סמיכה. The offering of a gentile and the offering of a friend come from one פסוק, so one word is left over to include partners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to understand רבי יהודה. In this answer he includes partners too, and still has a word left to exclude an heir.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, each קרבנו excluded one person: the gentile, the friend, and the heir. Here רבי יהודה learns the gentile and the friend from one word together. That leaves one word for the heir and one word for partners.

keyTerms.meaning: 'if you want, say…', introducing a second answer
really, actually
a פסוק, here meaning one appearance of the word
is left over, is free to teach something else

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
he really does hold it,
and the offering of a gentile and the offering of his friend
are learned from one verse,
phrases.notes: Both of these exclusions were mentioned in step 11, one from each קרבנו.

phrases.english: so one is left over for him
to include partners in סמיכה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second explanation of רבי יהודה, as an alternative to step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Combining two lessons into one word to free up another
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי יהודה uses all three mentions of קרבנו for a gentile, a friend and a father, it seemed he has no source to include partners in סמיכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה can learn the gentile and the friend from one קרבנו, which leaves a word to include partners.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the dispute about an heir does not have to depend on the question of partners.

steps.title: What is רבי מאיר's source that an heir can do תמורה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי מאיר holds that an heir can do תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר, who says an heir can do תמורה, what is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves from סמיכה to תמורה. It asks for the source of רבי מאיר's ruling that an heir can do תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה learned 'no תמורה' from 'no סמיכה' (step 9). רבי מאיר holds that an heir can do תמורה, so he needs his own source for it.

keyTerms.meaning: does תמורה, tries to swap a new animal for a קרבן
substitution: trying to swap a קרבן for another animal, which makes the new animal holy too

phrases.english: And רבי מאיר, who says an heir can do תמורה,
what is his reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּאָמַר יוֹרֵשׁ מֵמִיר, מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing with סמיכה, the גמרא returns to the second half of the dispute: תמורה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for רבי מאיר's view that an heir can do תמורה.

steps.title: הָמֵר יָמִיר includes the heir
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר learns from the doubled phrase הָמֵר יָמִיר that an heir can also do תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: 'If he shall surely substitute' comes to include the heir.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי מאיר learns it from the doubled word in the פסוק. The doubling adds the heir into the rule of תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have said just 'if he substitutes'. Instead it repeats the verb (הָמֵר יָמִיר), and רבי מאיר reads the extra word as including an heir.

keyTerms.meaning: 'if he shall surely substitute', the verb written twice in the פסוק
the ruling that an heir can do תמורה

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: an heir does סמיכה, because the third קרבנו is used for partners, and an heir does תמורה, from הָמֵר יָמִיר. רבי יהודה: an heir does neither.

phrases.english: He would tell you:
'If he shall surely substitute'
comes to include the heir,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: ״אִם הָמֵר יָמִיר״ לְרַבּוֹת הַיּוֹרֵשׁ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The doubled verb הָמֵר יָמִיר comes to include an heir in תמורה.
